label: copy-phase input "s" (very sparse, context-dependent)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.035% of steps). About 68% of activation mass is on steps whose input is the letter s, mostly during the copy phase (when s is fed back as the model output). It is strongest at recall_idx 1, i.e. when s was the first original token and is being fed back right after <DEL> (first_tok s 8.7x lift). It fires on only about 1.6% of copy-phase s inputs, so some unidentified context gates it. Activation is enriched when the previous input is <DEL>, k, t or u and when the current output is i, 3 or r, but adding these conditions only brings F1 to about 0.2. The remaining ~30% of mass falls on r, d, b, e, z inputs late in the original phase (orig_idx 3-6) of sequences that start with i (for example i i g g n m [r]). It never fires at t=0,1, on the delimiter step, or on most letters. Magnitude is small (mean 0.12) and does not follow any variable I checked.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=s (+4.89), in_tok=r (+4.01), orig0=i (+3.81), phase=2 & out_tok=3 (+3.34), phase=2 & out_tok=i (+3.33), prev_tok=k (+3.32). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.01), prev_tok=f (-2.80), prev_tok=i (-2.61), to_go=7 (-1.85).
